questions.text: संक्रमण तत्वों की 3d श्रेणी में बढ़ती हुई ऑक्सीकारक क्षमता का सही क्रम है :
questions.text_english: The correct order for the increasing oxidizing power in 3d series of transition elements is :
questions.solution: Option (C) is correct: VO2⁺ < Cr2O7²⁻ < MnO4⁻. The oxidizing power increases with the oxidation state and stability of the lower oxidation state. VO2⁺ contains V in +5 state but is a mild oxidizer; Cr2O7²⁻ with Cr in +6 is a stronger oxidizer; MnO4⁻ with Mn in +7 is the strongest oxidizing agent among these three because Mn readily accepts electrons to reach the stable +2 state. Options A, B, and D incorrectly place MnO4⁻ as a weaker oxidizer than Cr2O7²⁻, which is contrary to experimental evidence.
questions.topic: Oxidizing power of transition metal oxoanions

questions.text: संकुल [CoCl2(en)2]⁺ द्वारा दर्शाई समावयवता का प्रकार है :
questions.text_english: The type of isomerism shown by the complex [CoCl2(en)2]⁺ is :
questions.solution: Option (B) Geometrical isomerism is correct. The complex [CoCl2(en)2]⁺ has an octahedral geometry with two bidentate en (ethylenediamine) ligands and two Cl⁻ ligands. The two Cl⁻ ligands can be arranged either adjacent to each other (cis) or opposite to each other (trans), giving rise to cis-trans (geometrical) isomers. Linkage isomerism requires an ambidentate ligand; coordination isomerism requires both cation and anion to be complex ions; ionization isomerism requires exchange of ligand and counter ion — none of these apply here.
questions.topic: Types of isomerism in coordination compounds

questions.text: निम्नलिखित संकरण अवस्थाओं में से कौन-सा निम्न प्रचक्रण संकुल से संबद्ध है ?
questions.text_english: Which one of the following hybrid states is associated with low spin complex ?
questions.solution: Option (D) d²sp³ is correct. In low spin (inner orbital) octahedral complexes, the inner d-orbitals (3d) are used for hybridization along with s and p orbitals, giving d²sp³ hybridization. This occurs when strong field ligands force electron pairing. In contrast, sp³d² hybridization (option C) corresponds to high spin (outer orbital) octahedral complexes where 4d orbitals are used. sp³ (option B) corresponds to tetrahedral complexes, and sp³d (option A) corresponds to trigonal bipyramidal complexes.
questions.topic: Hybridization and spin state of complexes

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से किसे गरम करके ब्यूटेननाइट्राइल विरचित किया जा सकता है ?
questions.text_english: Butanenitrile may be prepared by heating :
questions.solution: Option (A) propyl chloride with KCN is correct. Butanenitrile (CH3CH2CH2CN) has 4 carbon atoms. When propyl chloride (CH3CH2CH2Cl, 3 carbons) reacts with KCN, the CN⁻ ion acts as a nucleophile and substitutes the Cl, adding one carbon to give butanenitrile (4 carbons). The reaction proceeds via SN2 mechanism. Butyl chloride (option B) would give pentanenitrile (5 carbons). Alcohols (options C and D) do not undergo this nucleophilic substitution with KCN under these conditions.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा सर्वाधिक अम्लीय है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is most acidic ?
questions.image_description: Four structural formulas shown: (A) phenol - benzene ring with OH; (B) benzyl alcohol - benzene ring with CH2OH; (C) cyclohexanol - cyclohexane ring with OH; (D) p-nitrophenol - benzene ring with OH and NO2 at para position.
questions.solution: Option (D) p-Nitrophenol is most acidic. The nitro group (–NO2) at the para position is a strong electron-withdrawing group. It stabilizes the phenoxide ion (conjugate base) through resonance and inductive effect by dispersing the negative charge, thereby increasing acidity. Plain phenol (A) is acidic due to resonance stabilization of phenoxide but less so than p-nitrophenol. Benzyl alcohol (B) and cyclohexanol (C) are simple alcohols with much higher pKa values (~15–16) compared to phenols (~10), making them far less acidic.

questions.text: HI के साथ अभिक्रिया करके (CH3)2CH–O–CH3 देता है :
questions.text_english: (CH3)2 CH–O–CH3 reacts with HI to give :
questions.solution: Option (B) is correct: (CH3)2CH–OH + CH3–I. When an unsymmetrical ether reacts with HI, the iodide ion (I⁻) attacks the less hindered (smaller) alkyl group via SN2 mechanism. Here, CH3– is the smaller group, so I⁻ attacks the methyl carbon to give CH3I (methyl iodide) and (CH3)2CHOH (isopropanol). Option (C) would be the product only if I⁻ attacked the bulkier isopropyl group, which is disfavoured. Option (D) would require two equivalents of HI, and option (A) shows no HI reaction at all.

questions.text: C3H8O आण्विक सूत्र के यौगिक (X) को किसी दूसरे यौगिक (Y) में प्रबल ऑक्सीकरण कर्मकों द्वारा ऑक्सीकृत किया जा सकता है, जिसका आण्विक सूत्र C3H6O2 है । यौगिक (X) है :
questions.text_english: A compound (X) with the molecular formula C3H8O can be oxidized by strong oxidizing agents to another compound (Y) whose molecular formula is C3H6O2. The compound (X) is :

options.D: उपर्युक्त में से कोई नहीं / None of the above

questions.solution: Option (C) CH3–CH2–CH2–OH (propan-1-ol) is correct. A primary alcohol on oxidation with strong oxidizing agents gives a carboxylic acid. Propan-1-ol (C3H8O) is oxidized to propanoic acid (C3H6O2), which matches compound Y. Propan-2-ol (option B), a secondary alcohol, would give a ketone (acetone, C3H6O), not a carboxylic acid of formula C3H6O2. Ethers (option A) are generally resistant to oxidation. Option (D) is therefore incorrect since option C satisfies all conditions.

questions.text: 10 mL ऐसीटोन को 50 mL क्लोरोफॉर्म के साथ मिलाने पर विलयन का कुल आयतन होगा :
questions.text_english: On mixing 10 mL of acetone with 50 mL of chloroform, the total volume of the solution will be :
questions.solution: Option (A) less than 60 mL is correct. Acetone and chloroform form a non-ideal solution showing negative deviation from Raoult's law. This is because hydrogen bonding occurs between the carbonyl oxygen of acetone and the hydrogen of chloroform (CHCl3), which is stronger than the interactions in the pure components. This strong interaction causes the molecules to come closer together, resulting in a contraction in volume. Therefore, the total volume of the mixture is less than the sum of individual volumes (10 + 50 = 60 mL).
questions.topic: Non-ideal solutions and volume change on mixing

questions.text: सेल स्थिरांक की इकाई है :
questions.text_english: The unit of cell constant is :
questions.solution: Option (C) cm⁻¹ is correct. The cell constant (G*) is defined as the ratio of distance between electrodes (l) to the area of cross-section of electrodes (A), i.e., G* = l/A. Since l has units of cm and A has units of cm², the unit of cell constant is cm/cm² = cm⁻¹. Option (A) is the unit of resistivity, option (B) is the unit of conductance, and option (D) is the unit of molar conductivity.

questions.text: किसी अभिक्रिया R → उत्पाद के लिए, log [R] एवं समय के मध्य ग्राफ खींचने पर एक सरल रेखा प्राप्त होती है जिसकी ढाल –1·25 s⁻¹ है । अभिक्रिया की कोटि है :
questions.text_english: For a certain reaction R → products, a plot of log [R] vs. time gives a straight line with a slope of –1·25 s⁻¹. The order of the reaction is :
questions.solution: Option (A) First order is correct. For a first order reaction, the integrated rate law is log[R] = log[R]₀ – (k/2.303)t. A plot of log[R] versus time gives a straight line with slope = –k/2.303. Since a straight line is obtained, the reaction is first order. The negative slope confirms the reactant concentration is decreasing with time. For a zero order reaction, [R] vs. time (not log[R]) gives a straight line; for second order, 1/[R] vs. time gives a straight line.
questions.topic: Integrated rate law and order determination from graphs

questions.text: किसी शून्य कोटि अभिक्रिया A → उत्पाद के लिए t₁/₂ है : (जहाँ [A]₀ = अभिकारक की प्रारम्भिक सांद्रता, k = वेग स्थिरांक)
questions.text_english: For a zero order reaction A → products, t₁/₂ is : (where [A]₀ = initial concentration of the reactant, k = rate constant)
questions.solution: Option (D) [A]₀/2k is correct. For a zero order reaction, the integrated rate law is [A] = [A]₀ – kt. At half-life (t₁/₂), [A] = [A]₀/2. Substituting: [A]₀/2 = [A]₀ – k·t₁/₂, which gives k·t₁/₂ = [A]₀/2, therefore t₁/₂ = [A]₀/2k. Option (B) is the half-life formula for first order reactions; option (C) is related to second order reactions; option (A) would give the time for complete consumption of reactant in zero order reaction.

questions.text: किसी अवाष्पशील विलेय के जलीय विलयन के वाष्प दाब का आपेक्षिक अवनमन 0·0225 है । अवाष्पशील विलेय का मोल-अंश है :
questions.text_english: The relative lowering of vapour pressure of an aqueous solution containing non-volatile solute is 0·0225. The mole fraction of the non-volatile solute is :
questions.solution: Option (D) 0·0225 is correct. According to Raoult's law, the relative lowering of vapour pressure equals the mole fraction of the solute: (P° – P)/P° = x₂ (mole fraction of solute). Since the relative lowering of vapour pressure is directly given as 0·0225, the mole fraction of the non-volatile solute is also 0·0225. This is a direct application of Raoult's law. The mole fraction of the solvent would then be 1 – 0·0225 = 0·9775.
questions.topic: Relative lowering of vapour pressure and Raoult's law

questions.solution: Option (A) is correct. Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion. In aniline, the lone pair of nitrogen is delocalized into the benzene ring through resonance, making it less available for donation to a proton (acid). This resonance stabilization of aniline reduces its basicity compared to cyclohexylamine, where the lone pair on nitrogen is not involved in any resonance and is fully available for protonation. Thus, cyclohexylamine is a stronger base (pKb ~ 3.36) than aniline (pKb ~ 9.38), and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.solution: Option (A) is correct. Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion. Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is a water-soluble vitamin. This is precisely why Vitamin C cannot accumulate in the body and must be consumed regularly through diet. The reason thus directly and correctly explains why the assertion is true.

Reason (R): Ammonolysis of alkyl halides mainly produces secondary amines.

questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. Assertion (A) is true — ammonolysis of alkyl halides does involve reacting the alkyl halide with an ethanolic solution of ammonia (NH3 in ethanol). However, Reason (R) is false — ammonolysis of alkyl halides primarily produces a mixture of primary amine (major product when excess NH3 is used), secondary amine, tertiary amine, and quaternary ammonium salt due to the successive alkylation of ammonia. The main/primary product when excess ammonia is used is the primary amine, not the secondary amine. Therefore, while the assertion is correct, the reason is incorrect.

questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. Assertion (A) is true — aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction. This is because the amino group (–NH2) of aniline acts as a Lewis base and reacts with the Lewis acid catalyst (AlCl3), forming a salt (C6H5NH2·AlCl3). This deactivates the ring by converting the electron-donating –NH2 into an electron-withdrawing –NH3⁺ group, preventing the electrophilic attack. However, Reason (R) is false — Friedel-Crafts reaction is an electrophilic aromatic substitution (EAS) reaction, NOT a nucleophilic substitution reaction. Therefore, the assertion is true but the reason is incorrect.

sub_questions.text_english:
Which one of the following pairs of substances undergoes SN1 reaction faster and why?
CH3–CH2–CH2–Cl  OR  CH2=CH–CH2–Cl

key_points: CH2=CH–CH2–Cl (allyl chloride) undergoes SN1 faster
Allyl carbocation is stabilized by resonance with the double bond
n-propyl chloride forms a primary carbocation with no resonance stabilization

sub_questions.solution: CH2=CH–CH2–Cl (allyl chloride) undergoes SN1 reaction faster. In SN1 reaction, the rate-determining step is the formation of a carbocation. When allyl chloride ionizes, it forms an allylic carbocation (CH2=CH–CH2⁺) which is stabilized by resonance — the positive charge is delocalized over two carbon atoms (CH2=CH–CH2⁺ ↔ ⁺CH2–CH=CH2). This resonance stabilization lowers the activation energy. In contrast, n-propyl chloride (CH3CH2CH2Cl) forms a primary carbocation with no resonance stabilization, making it much less stable and hence slower to react via SN1.

sub_questions.text_english: Write the major product: p-chloronitrobenzene treated with (i) NaOH, 443 K (ii) H⁺

key_points: p-Nitrophenol is the major product
The NO2 group at para position activates the ring towards nucleophilic substitution
OH⁻ replaces Cl at the activated position

sub_questions.solution: The major product is p-Nitrophenol (4-nitrophenol). The chlorine in p-chloronitrobenzene is activated towards nucleophilic aromatic substitution (SNAr) by the electron-withdrawing nitro group at the para position, which stabilizes the Meisenheimer complex intermediate. Treatment with NaOH at 443 K followed by acidification (H⁺) gives p-nitrophenol. The –NO2 group at the para position strongly activates the C–Cl bond towards nucleophilic attack by OH⁻.

sub_questions.text_english: What is lanthanoid contraction? Why is actinoid contraction greater from element to element than lanthanoid contraction?

key_points: Lanthanoid contraction: steady decrease in atomic/ionic radii across lanthanoids due to imperfect shielding by 4f electrons
Actinoid contraction is greater because 5f orbitals have even poorer shielding than 4f orbitals
5f electrons shield the nucleus less effectively than 4f electrons

sub_questions.solution: Lanthanoid contraction refers to the steady decrease in the atomic and ionic radii of lanthanoid elements (La to Lu) with increasing atomic number. This happens because, as protons are added to the nucleus, the poorly shielding 4f electrons fail to screen the outer electrons from the increased nuclear charge effectively, causing a gradual contraction. Actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than lanthanoid contraction because 5f orbitals are even more poorly shielded than 4f orbitals — the 5f electrons have a more diffuse shape and screen nuclear charge less effectively, resulting in a larger contraction per element.

sub_questions.text_english: Why do transition metals have high enthalpy of atomization? Which element of 3d-series has lowest enthalpy of atomization?

key_points: Transition metals have strong metallic bonding due to involvement of both (n-1)d and ns electrons
High number of unpaired d electrons leads to stronger interatomic bonding
Zinc (Zn) has the lowest enthalpy of atomization in the 3d series

sub_questions.solution: Transition metals show high enthalpy of atomization because both (n–1)d and ns electrons participate in metallic bonding. The presence of unpaired d electrons allows for stronger and more extensive interatomic bonding through delocalization. Greater the number of unpaired electrons, stronger the metallic bonds and higher the enthalpy of atomization. Among the 3d series, Zinc (Zn) has the lowest enthalpy of atomization because its d-orbitals are completely filled (3d¹⁰ 4s²), leaving no unpaired d electrons available for metallic bonding, which weakens the intermetallic interactions.

किसी प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया का वेग स्थिरांक 1·25 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹ है । इस अभिकर्मक के 5 g को 2·5 g में घटने में कितना समय लगेगा ?
[ log 2 = 0·301, log 3 = 0·4771, log 4 = 0·6021 ]
questions.text_english:
A first order reaction has a rate constant 1·25 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. How long will 5 g of this reactant take to reduce to 2·5 g ?
[ log 2 = 0·301, log 3 = 0·4771, log 4 = 0·6021 ]
questions.solution: For a first order reaction, the integrated rate law is: t = (2.303/k) × log([A]₀/[A]). Here, [A]₀ = 5 g, [A] = 2.5 g, k = 1.25 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. Therefore, t = (2.303 / 1.25 × 10⁻³) × log(5/2.5) = (2.303 / 1.25 × 10⁻³) × log 2 = (2.303 × 0.301) / 1.25 × 10⁻³ = 0.6931 / 1.25 × 10⁻³ = 554.4 s ≈ 554 s. The reactant reduces from 5 g to 2.5 g (half its initial amount) in approximately 554 seconds.

questions.text: ग्लूकोस (मोलर द्रव्यमान = 180 g mol⁻¹) का 3% विलयन किसी अज्ञात कार्बनिक पदार्थ के 2·5% विलयन के साथ समपरासारी है । अज्ञात कार्बनिक पदार्थ का अणु भार परिकलित कीजिए ।
questions.text_english: A 3% solution of glucose (molar mass = 180 g mol⁻¹) is isotonic with 2·5% solution of an unknown organic substance. Calculate the molecular weight of the unknown organic substance.

key_points: Isotonic solutions have equal osmotic pressure and equal molarity
Molarity of glucose = (30 g/L) / 180 = 0.1667 mol/L
Molarity of unknown = 25 g/L / M₂ = 0.1667 → M₂ = 150 g/mol

questions.solution: Since the two solutions are isotonic, they have equal osmotic pressure, which means equal molar concentrations. For glucose: 3% solution means 3 g per 100 mL = 30 g per litre. Molarity of glucose = 30/180 = 1/6 mol/L. For the unknown substance: 2.5% solution means 2.5 g per 100 mL = 25 g per litre. Since molarity must be equal, 25/M₂ = 1/6, therefore M₂ = 25 × 6 = 150 g mol⁻¹. The molecular weight of the unknown organic substance is 150 g mol⁻¹.

questions.text_english:
Give the equations of reactions for the preparation of: (any three)
(a) Phenol from chlorobenzene
(b) Salicylaldehyde from phenol
(c) 2-Methoxyacetophenone from anisole
(d) Picric acid from phenol

key_points: (a) C6H5Cl + NaOH (300°C, 300 atm) → C6H5ONa + HCl; then C6H5ONa + HCl → C6H5OH + NaCl (Dow's process)
(b) Phenol + CHCl3 + NaOH (Reimer-Tiemann reaction) → 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde)
(c) Anisole + CH3COCl / AlCl3 (Friedel-Crafts acylation) → 2-methoxyacetophenone (ortho product major)
(d) Phenol + conc. HNO3/H2SO4 (nitration with excess) → 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid)

questions.solution:
Any three of the following reactions:

(a) Chlorobenzene to Phenol (Dow's process): C6H5Cl is heated with NaOH at 300°C under 300 atm pressure to give sodium phenoxide (C6H5ONa), which on acidification gives phenol: C6H5Cl + 2NaOH → C6H5ONa + NaCl + H2O; C6H5ONa + HCl → C6H5OH + NaCl.

(b) Salicylaldehyde from Phenol (Reimer-Tiemann reaction): Phenol is treated with CHCl3 in the presence of NaOH, followed by acidification: C6H5OH + CHCl3 + 3NaOH → 2-HO–C6H4–CHO (salicylaldehyde) + 3NaCl + 2H2O.

(c) 2-Methoxyacetophenone from Anisole (Friedel-Crafts acylation): Anisole (C6H5OCH3) reacts with acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) in the presence of AlCl3 to give predominantly 2-methoxyacetophenone: C6H5OCH3 + CH3COCl → 2-CH3O–C6H4–COCH3 + HCl (ortho product is major due to steric and electronic effects).

(d) Picric acid from Phenol: Phenol is treated with concentrated HNO3/H2SO4 (nitrating mixture) to give 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid): C6H5OH + 3HNO3 (conc) → 2,4,6-(NO2)3C6H2OH + 3H2O.

(क) क्लोरीन यद्यपि इलेक्ट्रॉन अपनयक समूह है फिर भी यह ऐरोमैटिक इलेक्ट्रॉनरागी प्रतिस्थापन अभिक्रियाओं में ऑर्थो/पैरा निर्देशक है ।
(ख) रेसिमिक मिश्रण ध्रुवण अघूर्णक होता है ।
(ग) n-प्रोपिल क्लोराइड की अपेक्षा ऐलिल क्लोराइड अधिक शीघ्रता से जल-अपघटित हो जाता है ।
questions.text_english:
Give reasons for the following:
(a) Chlorine is ortho/para directing in electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions, though chlorine is an electron withdrawing group.
(b) Racemic mixture is optically inactive.
(c) Allyl chloride is hydrolysed more readily than n-propyl chloride.

key_points: (a) Cl donates lone pair into ring via resonance (o/p director) despite –I inductive effect
(b) Racemic mixture contains equal amounts of d and l forms that rotate plane-polarized light by equal and opposite amounts, cancelling each other
(c) Allyl chloride forms a resonance-stabilized allylic carbocation, facilitating SN1; n-propyl chloride forms an unstable primary carbocation

questions.solution:
(a) Although chlorine withdraws electrons by induction (–I effect), it donates a lone pair of electrons to the benzene ring through resonance (+M effect). This resonance donation increases the electron density at ortho and para positions relative to Cl. Since the +M effect of resonance donation dominates over the –I effect for directing purposes, chlorine acts as an ortho/para director in EAS reactions, even though it deactivates the ring overall.

(b) A racemic mixture contains equimolar amounts of two enantiomers (d-form and l-form). The d-form rotates the plane of plane-polarized light to the right by a certain angle, while the l-form rotates it by the same angle to the left. These equal and opposite rotations cancel each other out, making the racemic mixture optically inactive (net rotation = 0°).

(c) Allyl chloride (CH2=CH–CH2–Cl) hydrolyses more readily because it ionizes to form an allylic carbocation (CH2=CH–CH2⁺), which is resonance-stabilized. The positive charge is delocalized over two carbon atoms, lowering the activation energy. n-Propyl chloride forms an unstable primary carbocation with no resonance stabilization, making hydrolysis much slower.

questions.text: 283 K पर किसी विलायक का वाष्प दाब 100 mm Hg है । उस तनु विलयन का वाष्प दाब परिकलित कीजिए जिसमें 283 K पर किसी प्रबल विद्युत-अपघट्य AB का 1 मोल विलायक के 50 मोल में घुला है (यह मान लीजिए कि विलेय AB पूर्णतः वियोजित हो जाता है) ।
questions.text_english: The vapour pressure of a solvent at 283 K is 100 mm Hg. Calculate the vapour pressure of a dilute solution containing 1 mole of a strong electrolyte AB in 50 moles of the solvent at 283 K (assuming complete dissociation of solute AB).

key_points: AB → A⁺ + B⁻ (i = 2, complete dissociation)
Total moles of solute particles = 2; moles of solvent = 50
(P° – P)/P° = n_solute / (n_solute + n_solvent) = 2/52

questions.solution: Since AB is a strong electrolyte and completely dissociates, AB → A⁺ + B⁻. So 1 mole of AB gives 2 moles of ions. Total moles of solute particles = 2, moles of solvent = 50. Using Raoult's law: (P° – P)/P° = x_solute = n_solute/(n_solute + n_solvent) = 2/(2 + 50) = 2/52. Therefore, (100 – P)/100 = 2/52. Solving: 100 – P = 200/52 = 3.846. P = 100 – 3.846 = 96.15 mm Hg. The vapour pressure of the dilute solution is approximately 96.15 mm Hg.

questions.text:

[दिया गया है : 2·303 R = 19·15 JK⁻¹ mol⁻¹, log 3 = 0·48]
questions.text_english:
The rate of a gaseous reaction triples when temperature is increased from 17°C to 27°C. Calculate the energy of activation for this reaction.
[Given: 2·303 R = 19·15 JK⁻¹ mol⁻¹, log 3 = 0·48]
questions.solution: Given: T1 = 17 + 273 = 290 K, T2 = 27 + 273 = 300 K, k2/k1 = 3. Using the Arrhenius equation: log(k2/k1) = (Ea/2.303R) × (T2 – T1)/(T1 × T2). Substituting: log 3 = (Ea/19.15) × (300 – 290)/(290 × 300). 0.48 = (Ea/19.15) × (10/87000). Ea = 0.48 × 19.15 × 87000/10 = 0.48 × 19.15 × 8700 = 79,898.4 J/mol ≈ 79.9 kJ/mol. The activation energy for this reaction is approximately 79.9 kJ mol⁻¹.

निम्नलिखित सेल का वि.वा. बल (emf) परिकलित कीजिए :
Zn (s) | Zn²⁺ (0·1 M) || Sn²⁺ (0·001 M) | Sn (s)
दिया गया है : E°Zn²⁺/Zn = –0·76 V, E°Sn²⁺/Sn = –0·14 V
[ log 10 = 1 ]
questions.text_english:
Calculate emf of the following cell:
Zn (s) | Zn²⁺ (0·1 M) || Sn²⁺ (0·001 M) | Sn (s)
Given: E°Zn²⁺/Zn = –0·76 V, E°Sn²⁺/Sn = –0·14 V
[ log 10 = 1 ]

key_points: E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = –0.14 – (–0.76) = +0.62 V
Nernst equation: E = E° – (0.0591/n) × log([Zn²⁺]/[Sn²⁺])

questions.solution: Zn is the anode (oxidation) and Sn is the cathode (reduction). E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = –0.14 – (–0.76) = +0.62 V. Using the Nernst equation (n = 2 electrons transferred): E_cell = E°cell – (0.0591/n) × log Q, where Q = [Zn²⁺]/[Sn²⁺] = 0.1/0.001 = 100 = 10². E_cell = 0.62 – (0.0591/2) × log(100) = 0.62 – (0.02955) × 2 = 0.62 – 0.0591 = 0.5609 V ≈ 0.56 V. The emf of the cell is approximately 0.56 V.

निम्नलिखित से संबद्ध अभिक्रिया लिखिए :
(क) वोल्फ-किश्नर अपचयन
(ख) विकार्बोक्सिलन अभिक्रिया
(ग) कैनिज़ारो अभिक्रिया
questions.text_english:
Write the reaction involved in the following:
(a) Wolff-Kishner reduction
(b) Decarboxylation reaction
(c) Cannizzaro reaction

key_points: (a) Wolff-Kishner: RCHO + H2N-NH2/KOH/ethylene glycol/heat → RCH3 + N2 + H2O
(b) Decarboxylation: RCOONa + NaOH (CaO, heat) → RH + Na2CO3
(c) Cannizzaro: 2HCHO + NaOH → HCOO⁻Na⁺ + CH3OH

questions.solution:
(a) Wolff-Kishner Reduction: Carbonyl compounds (aldehydes or ketones) are reduced to hydrocarbons by heating with hydrazine (H2N–NH2) in the presence of KOH (base) in ethylene glycol. Example: R–CHO + H2N–NH2 → R–CH=N–NH2 (hydrazone); then KOH/heat → R–CH3 + N2↑ + H2O. The carbonyl group is converted to a –CH2– group.

(b) Decarboxylation Reaction: Sodium salt of a carboxylic acid is heated with sodalime (NaOH + CaO) to give an alkane with one fewer carbon atom and sodium carbonate. Example: CH3COONa + NaOH (CaO, heat) → CH4 + Na2CO3.

(c) Cannizzaro Reaction: Aldehydes lacking alpha-hydrogen atoms undergo self oxidation-reduction (disproportionation) in the presence of concentrated NaOH. One molecule is oxidized to carboxylate salt and the other is reduced to an alcohol. Example: 2HCHO + NaOH (conc.) → HCOONa (sodium formate) + CH3OH (methanol).

questions.text: कार्बोहाइड्रेट पौधों और प्राणियों दोनों में जीवन के लिए आवश्यक होते हैं । पौधों में स्टार्च की तरह और प्राणियों में ग्लाइकोजन के रूप में कार्बोहाइड्रेट संग्रहण अणुओं की भाँति प्रयुक्त होते हैं । रासायनिक रूप से ये पॉलिहाइड्रॉक्सी ऐल्डिहाइड अथवा कीटोन होते हैं । कार्बोहाइड्रेटों को जल-अपघटन में उनके व्यवहार के आधार पर मोनोसैकैराइड, ओलिगोसैकैराइड और पॉलिसैकैराइड में वर्गीकृत किया गया है । सभी मोनोसैकैराइड अपचायी शर्करा होती हैं, अर्थात् ये टॉलेन अभिकर्मक तथा फेलिंग विलयन से ऑक्सीकृत हो जाती हैं । ग्लूकोस जैसा मोनोसैकैराइड ऐल्डोहैक्सोज होता है और इसका आण्विक सूत्र C6H12O6 पाया गया । विभिन्न अभिकर्मकों जैसे HI, H2N–OH, ब्रोमीन जल, (CH3CO)2O इत्यादि के साथ अभिक्रिया करके इसकी संरचना में एक ऐल्डिहाइड समूह, एक प्राथमिक ऐल्कोहॉलिक समूह (–CH2OH) और चार द्वितीयक ऐल्कोहॉलिक समूह (>CHOH) पाए गए । ऐल्डिहाइड समूह उपस्थित होते हुए भी ग्लूकोस ऐल्डिहाइड समूह की कुछ अभिक्रियाएँ जैसे शिफ परीक्षण, NaHSO3 योगज नहीं देता है । यह ग्लूकोस के दो चक्रीय हैमीऐसीटैल रूपों के अस्तित्व को समझाता है जिनमें भिन्नता केवल C–1 पर उपस्थित हाइड्रॉक्सिल समूह के विन्यास में होती है ।
questions.text_english: Carbohydrates are essential for life in both plants and animals. Carbohydrates are used as storage molecules as starch in plants and glycogen in animals. Chemically they are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones. On the basis of their behaviour on hydrolysis, carbohydrates are classified as monosaccharides, oligosaccharides and polysaccharides. All monosaccharides are reducing sugars, i.e., they are oxidized by Tollens' reagent and Fehling's solution. A monosaccharide like glucose is aldohexose and its molecular formula was found to be C6H12O6. After reacting with different reagents like HI, H2N–OH, Bromine water, (CH3CO)2O, etc. its structure was found to contain one aldehyde group, one primary alcoholic group, (–CH2OH) and four secondary alcoholic groups (>CHOH). Despite having the aldehyde group, glucose does not give some of the reactions of aldehyde group like Schiff's test, NaHSO3 addition. This explains the existence of glucose in two cyclic hemiacetal forms which differ only in the configuration of the hydroxyl group at C–1.

sub_questions.text_english: On what basis can we say that Cu is a transition element but Zn is not? (Atomic number: Cu = 29, Zn = 30)

key_points: Cu in Cu²⁺ state has incomplete d-subshell (3d⁹); Zn has completely filled d-subshell in all oxidation states (3d¹⁰)

sub_questions.solution: Cu (Z=29) has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹. In its common ion Cu²⁺, the configuration is [Ar] 3d⁹, which has an incomplete d-subshell. Therefore, Cu is classified as a transition element. Zn (Z=30) has the configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s², and its ion Zn²⁺ has the configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰ — a completely filled d-subshell in all its oxidation states. Since a transition element is defined as one that has an incomplete d-subshell in the elemental state or in any of its common ionic states, Zn does not qualify.

sub_questions.text: संक्रमण तत्व ऑक्सीकरण अवस्थाओं में विविधता क्यों दर्शाते हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why do transition elements show variety of oxidation states?

key_points: (n-1)d and ns electrons have similar energies and can both participate in bonding

sub_questions.solution: Transition elements show a variety of oxidation states because both (n–1)d and ns electrons have comparable energies and can participate in bond formation. As the energy difference between these orbitals is small, electrons from both subshells can be lost. For example, iron (Fe) shows +2 (losing 4s² electrons) and +3 (losing 4s² and one 3d electron) oxidation states. The gradual increase in nuclear charge across the series also contributes to the stability of various oxidation states.

(ii) Complete the following ionic equation: 2MnO4²⁻ + H2O + I⁻ →

key_points: Main (i): Irregular E° values due to irregular variation in ionization enthalpy, sublimation enthalpy, and hydration enthalpy
Main (ii): Transition metals show variable oxidation states differing by 1 (d electrons involved); non-transition elements show states differing by 2 (s electrons)
OR (i): Cr²⁺ (d⁴→d³, t₂g³ stable half-filled) is reducing; Mn³⁺ (d⁴→d⁵, Mn²⁺ with half-filled d⁵ is very stable) is oxidizing

OR (ii): 2MnO4²⁻ + H2O + I⁻ → 2MnO4⁻ + 2OH⁻ + I₂ (not balanced — actually: 2MnO4²⁻ + I⁻ + H2O → 2MnO4⁻ + I⁻ ... balanced: 2MnO4²⁻ + H2O + I⁻ → 2MnO4⁻ + 2OH⁻ + I₂ is incorrect. Correct: 2MnO4²⁻ + H2O → MnO4⁻ + MnO2 + 2OH⁻ is Cannizzaro; with I⁻: 2MnO4²⁻ + I⁻ + H2O → 2MnO4⁻ + I⁻ — not standard. Standard: 2MnO4⁻ + H2O + I⁻ is not the question; the equation given is 2MnO4²⁻. Balanced: 2MnO4²⁻ + I⁻ + H2O → 2MnO4⁻ + IO⁻ + 2OH⁻

sub_questions.solution:
Main option:
(i) The E°M²⁺/M values show an irregular trend from Vanadium to Zinc because E° depends on three factors: sublimation enthalpy (energy to convert solid metal to gaseous atoms), ionization enthalpy (energy to form M²⁺), and hydration enthalpy (energy released when M²⁺ is hydrated). These three factors vary irregularly across the transition series, resulting in the irregular trend of E° values.

(ii) Transition metals show variability in oxidation states that differ by 1 (e.g., Fe²⁺ and Fe³⁺, Cu⁺ and Cu²⁺), because d electrons are involved one at a time. Non-transition elements show oxidation states that differ by 2 (e.g., Pb²⁺ and Pb⁴⁺, Sn²⁺ and Sn⁴⁺), because they lose electrons from the s-subshell in pairs (inert pair effect).

OR option:
(i) Cr²⁺ has the configuration [Ar] 3d⁴. It tends to lose one more electron to reach the very stable half-filled 3d³ configuration (Cr³⁺: t₂g³), making Cr²⁺ a strong reducing agent. Mn³⁺ also has 3d⁴ configuration ([Ar] 3d⁴), and it readily gains one electron to reach the exceptionally stable half-filled 3d⁵ configuration of Mn²⁺, making Mn³⁺ a strong oxidizing agent.

(ii) 2MnO4²⁻ + H2O + I⁻ → 2MnO4⁻ + 2OH⁻ + I⁻ (net ionic). The balanced equation is: 2MnO4²⁻ + H2O + I⁻ → 2MnO4⁻ + 2OH⁻ + IO⁻ (periodate/iodate depending on conditions). Standard completion: 2MnO4²⁻ + I⁻ + H2O → 2MnO4⁻ + IO⁻ + 2OH⁻.

sub_questions.text_english: Why is oxidation of aldehydes easier as compared to ketones?

key_points: Aldehydes have a hydrogen atom on the carbonyl carbon which can be removed during oxidation
Ketones have no such hydrogen and require breaking C-C bonds for oxidation

sub_questions.solution: Aldehydes have a hydrogen atom directly attached to the carbonyl carbon (–CHO group), which is easily removed during oxidation to give a carboxylic acid. This H can be abstracted by mild oxidizing agents like Tollens' reagent or Fehling's solution. In ketones, both substituents on the carbonyl carbon are carbon groups (R–CO–R'), and there is no hydrogen on the carbonyl carbon. To oxidize a ketone, a C–C bond must be broken, which requires much stronger oxidizing agents and more energy. Therefore, aldehydes are much more easily oxidized than ketones.

sub_questions.text: ऐल्डिहाइडों के ऐल्फा (α) हाइड्रोजन परमाणुओं की प्रकृति अम्लीय क्यों होती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: Why are the alpha (α) hydrogen atoms of aldehydes acidic in nature?

key_points: The carbonyl group (C=O) is electron-withdrawing
Loss of α-H forms a carbanion (enolate) stabilized by resonance with the C=O group

sub_questions.solution: The alpha (α) hydrogen atoms in aldehydes are acidic because the adjacent carbonyl group (C=O) is strongly electron-withdrawing. When an α-hydrogen is removed, the resulting carbanion (enolate ion) is stabilized by resonance with the carbonyl group — the negative charge is delocalized over the α-carbon and the oxygen of the carbonyl group (–CH=C–O⁻ ↔ –CH–C=O). This resonance stabilization of the enolate ion makes the loss of α-hydrogen relatively easy, i.e., α-hydrogens are acidic (pKa ~17–20).

key_points: Tollens' test: ethanal gives silver mirror, ethanoic acid does not

sub_questions.solution: Sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) test: Add sodium carbonate solution to each compound. Ethanoic acid (acetic acid, CH3COOH) being an acid reacts with Na2CO3 to produce brisk effervescence due to the evolution of CO2 gas: 2CH3COOH + Na2CO3 → 2CH3COONa + H2O + CO2↑. Ethanal (CH3CHO) does not react with Na2CO3 and gives no effervescence. Alternatively, Tollens' test can be used: ethanal reduces Tollens' reagent to give a silver mirror, while ethanoic acid does not.

sub_questions.text_english: State Faraday's first law of electrolysis. How much charge in Faraday is required for the reduction of 1 mol of MnO4⁻ to Mn²⁺?

key_points: Faraday's first law: mass of substance deposited is proportional to quantity of electricity passed
MnO4⁻ (Mn in +7) → Mn²⁺ (Mn in +2): change = 5 electrons per formula unit
Charge required = 5 Faraday per mole

sub_questions.solution:
Faraday's First Law of Electrolysis: The mass of a substance deposited or dissolved at an electrode during electrolysis is directly proportional to the quantity of electricity (charge) passed through the electrolyte. Mathematically, m = Z × Q, where m is mass deposited, Z is electrochemical equivalent, and Q is the total charge passed.

For reduction of MnO4⁻ to Mn²⁺: In MnO4⁻, oxidation state of Mn is +7. In Mn²⁺, oxidation state is +2. Change in oxidation state = 7 – 2 = 5. Therefore, 5 electrons are required per MnO4⁻ ion. For 1 mole of MnO4⁻, 5 moles of electrons = 5 Faraday of charge are required.

sub_questions.text: 0·0025 mol L⁻¹ ऐसीटिक अम्ल की चालकता 5·25 × 10⁻⁵ S cm⁻¹ है। यदि ऐसीटिक अम्ल के लिए Λ°m का मान 390 S cm² mol⁻¹ है, तो इसकी वियोजन मात्रा का परिकलन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: The conductivity of 0·0025 mol L⁻¹ acetic acid is 5·25 × 10⁻⁵ S cm⁻¹. Calculate its degree of dissociation if Λ°m for acetic acid is 390 S cm² mol⁻¹.
sub_questions.solution: Molar conductivity Λm = (κ × 1000) / c = (5.25 × 10⁻⁵ × 1000) / 0.0025 = 0.0525 / 0.0025 = 21 S cm² mol⁻¹. Degree of dissociation α = Λm / Λ°m = 21 / 390 = 0.05385 ≈ 0.054 (or 5.4%). The degree of dissociation of acetic acid at this concentration is approximately 0.054 or 5.4%.

sub_questions.text: अष्टफलकीय संकुल की क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र विपाटन ऊर्जा (Δo) किस प्रकार चतुष्फलकीय संकुल की विपाटन ऊर्जा (Δt) से संबंधित है ?
sub_questions.text_english: How is the crystal field splitting energy for octahedral complex (Δo) related to that of tetrahedral complex (Δt)?

key_points: Δt = (4/9) Δo

sub_questions.solution: The crystal field splitting energy for a tetrahedral complex (Δt) is related to that of an octahedral complex (Δo) by the expression: Δt = (4/9) Δo. This means the splitting in a tetrahedral field is approximately 4/9 (about 44%) of that in an octahedral field with the same ligands and metal. The smaller splitting in tetrahedral complexes is because there are only 4 ligands (instead of 6) and none of them directly point along the d-orbital axes.

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित संकुल का IUPAC नाम लिखिए: [PtCl2(en)2](NO3)2
sub_questions.text_english: Write the IUPAC name of the following complex: [PtCl2(en)2](NO3)2

key_points: Dichloridobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)platinum(IV) nitrate

sub_questions.solution: The IUPAC name of [PtCl2(en)2](NO3)2 is: Dichloridobis(ethane-1,2-diamine)platinum(IV) nitrate. Here, the complex cation is [PtCl2(en)2]²⁺. The central metal is Pt. Ligands are 2 Cl⁻ (chlorido) and 2 en (ethane-1,2-diamine, a bidentate ligand, so bis is used). Oxidation state of Pt: 2(charge of en) + 2(–1 for Cl) + Pt = +2 charge of cation, so Pt = +4. Counter ion: 2 NO3⁻ (nitrate).

sub_questions.text: संयोजकता आबंध सिद्धांत (VBT) के आधार पर संकुल [Ni(CO)4] की ज्यामिति और चुंबकीय व्यवहार लिखिए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the geometry and magnetic behaviour of the complex [Ni(CO)4] on the basis of Valency Bond Theory (VBT).

key_points: Tetrahedral geometry with sp³ hybridization
Diamagnetic — all electrons paired after pairing by CO (strong field ligand)

sub_questions.solution: In [Ni(CO)4], Ni is in 0 oxidation state with configuration [Ar] 3d⁸ 4s². CO is a strong field ligand which causes pairing of the two unpaired 3d electrons, giving a 3d¹⁰ configuration. The four CO ligands use the 4s and three 4p orbitals (sp³ hybridization) for bond formation. Therefore, [Ni(CO)4] has a tetrahedral geometry. Since all electrons are paired after the rearrangement, the complex is diamagnetic (no unpaired electrons).

sub_questions.text: संकुल [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] के द्वारा किस प्रकार की समावयवता दर्शाई जाती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: What type of isomerism is shown by the complex [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6]?

key_points: Coordination isomerism

sub_questions.solution: The complex [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] shows coordination isomerism. In coordination isomerism, both the cation and anion are complex ions, and the isomers differ in the distribution of ligands between the two complex ions. Here, the cation is [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ and the anion is [Cr(CN)6]³⁻. The coordination isomer would be [Co(CN)6][Cr(NH3)6], where the ligands have been exchanged between the two metal centres.

sub_questions.text: क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत के आधार पर किसी उपसहसंयोजन यौगिक में d⁴ आयन का इलेक्ट्रॉनिक विन्यास लिखिए यदि Δo < P हो । क्या यह उपसहसंयोजन यौगिक उच्च प्रचक्रण अथवा निम्न प्रचक्रण संकुल है ?
sub_questions.text_english: For the coordination compound on the basis of crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration for d⁴ ion if Δo < P. Is the coordination compound a high spin or low spin complex?

key_points: Electronic configuration: t₂g³ eg¹ (one electron in each of the three t₂g and one in eg)
High spin complex

sub_questions.solution: When Δo < P (crystal field splitting energy is less than the pairing energy), it is energetically more favorable for electrons to occupy the higher energy eg orbitals rather than pairing in the lower t₂g orbitals. For a d⁴ ion in an octahedral field with Δo < P, the electronic configuration is t₂g³ eg¹ — three electrons singly occupy the t₂g orbitals and the fourth electron enters the eg orbital rather than pairing. This is a high spin complex because it has the maximum number of unpaired electrons (4 unpaired electrons). Weak field ligands such as F⁻, Cl⁻, H2O cause this situation.

sub_questions.text: [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ और [Co(NH3)4Cl2]⁺ में से कौन हेट्रोलेप्टिक संकुल है और क्यों ?
sub_questions.text_english: Out of [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ and [Co(NH3)4Cl2]⁺, which complex is heteroleptic and why?

key_points: [Co(NH3)4Cl2]⁺ is heteroleptic because it contains two different types of ligands (NH3 and Cl⁻)

sub_questions.solution: [Co(NH3)4Cl2]⁺ is the heteroleptic complex. A heteroleptic complex is one that contains two or more different types of ligands coordinated to the central metal atom. In [Co(NH3)4Cl2]⁺, cobalt is bonded to two different ligands — four NH3 (ammine) ligands and two Cl⁻ (chlorido) ligands. In contrast, [Co(NH3)6]³⁺ is a homoleptic complex because all six ligands are the same (only NH3).

sub_questions.text: [PtCl2(en)2]²⁺ के प्रकाशिक समावयवों की संरचनाएँ बनाइए ।
sub_questions.text_english: Draw the structures of optical isomers of [PtCl2(en)2]²⁺.

key_points: The cis-[PtCl2(en)2]²⁺ exists as two non-superimposable mirror images (Δ and Λ forms)
The trans isomer does not show optical isomerism

sub_questions.solution: In [PtCl2(en)2]²⁺, Pt is octahedral with two bidentate en ligands and two Cl⁻ ligands. The cis isomer (where the two Cl⁻ are on the same side) has a non-superimposable mirror image and hence shows optical isomerism. The two optical isomers are the d-form (Δ, right-handed) and l-form (Λ, left-handed), which are enantiomers that rotate plane-polarized light in opposite directions. The trans isomer (Cl⁻ on opposite sides) has a plane of symmetry and does not show optical isomerism. Structures: Δ-cis-[PtCl2(en)2]²⁺ and Λ-cis-[PtCl2(en)2]²⁺ — both have octahedral geometry with en chelating and Cl in cis positions, but twisted in opposite helical senses.
